official.title: Doctoral Researcher in Theoretical Quantum Materials
official.description_text:
Aalto University is where science and art meet technology and business. We shape a sustainable future by making research breakthroughs in and across our disciplines, sparking the game changers of tomorrow and creating novel solutions to major global challenges. Our community is made up of 16 000 students and 5 200 employees, including 446 professors. Our campus is in Espoo, Greater Helsinki, Finland.Diversity is part of who we are, and we actively work to ensure our community’s diversity and inclusiveness. This is why we warmly encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds to join our community.
At the Department of Applied Physics, our pioneering research in physical sciences creates important industrial applications that hold great technological potential. Our research focuses on Materials physics, Quantum technology, Soft & living matter, and Advanced energy solutions. Topics extend from fundamental research to important applications. We educate future generations of research and development professionals, data specialists, technology experts, inventors, and scientists for industry and society.
We invite applications for a
doctoral researcher
in theoretical condensed-matter physics at Aalto University’s Department of Applied Physics. The position is part of a Research Council of Finland fellowship project led by Dr. Tobias Wolf and focuses on interaction-driven phases in two-dimensional quantum materials.
Project Description
The doctoral researcher will investigate how electronic interactions give rise to collective phases in low-dimensional quantum materials. Systems of interest include rhombohedral multilayer graphene and moiré materials, which offer ways to study how competing orders, unconventional superconductivity, and topological phases emerge and how they can be distinguished experimentally. The researcher will develop microscopic models and use analytical and computational many-body methods suited to the scientific questions and their interests. The doctoral researcher will be part of the Correlated Quantum Materials (CQM) group led by Prof. José Lado and work under the supervision of RCF Fellow Dr. Tobias Wolf.
Requirements
We seek a motivated candidate with:
A master’s degree in physics or a closely related field (by the start of the PhD).
A solid foundation in quantum mechanics and condensed-matter physics.
Programming experience and an interest in combining theory and computation and connecting results to experiments.
Experience with many-body theory or numerical simulations is beneficial but not required.
Proficiency in English (Finnish is not required).
The Position Offers
Full-time, 4-year PhD funding through the Research Council of Finland. The position of Doctoral Researcher is initially filled for 2 years. The contract is continued for another 2 years after a successful midterm review.
Access to world-class computational resources Aalto Triton and Lumi and collaborative research environment at Aalto University.
Opportunities to collaborate with leading international groups (both theoretical and experimental groups).
Travel funding for international conferences and workshops.
A research visit to an international research group as part of the PhD project.
The annual workload of research and teaching staff at Aalto University is 1612 hours. Aalto University follows the salary system of Finnish universities. The starting salary is approximately 3142 €/month (gross), and it increases as the Doctoral Researcher progresses in the research and studies. The contract includes Aalto University occupational healthcare.
How to Apply
If you would like to be considered for the position, please submit your application in English through our recruitment system by clicking the link “Apply now!” on our webpage.
To apply, please share the following application materials with us:
A one-page motivation letter.
A CV.
Copies of academic transcripts and degree certificates.
Contact details for at least one academic referee.
Kindly apply before the deadline – 10.01.2027 at 23:59 (Finnish time).
Aalto University reserves the right for justified reasons to leave the position open, extend the application period, reopen the application process, and consider candidates who have not submitted applications during the application period.
Please note: Aalto University’s employees should apply for the position via our internal HR system Workday (Internal Jobs) by using their existing Workday user account (not via the external webpage for open positions). Aalto University’s students and visitors should apply as external candidates with personal (not Aalto) email.
More information
If you wish to hear more about the position, you can reach out to Dr. Tobias Wolf (
physics@wolft.net
).

January 10, 2027
Starting date:
Preferably May 2027 (or as agreed)

ai.summary: Doctoral position in theoretical condensed-matter physics focusing on interaction-driven phases in two-dimensional quantum materials (graphene, moiré materials). Work involves microscopic modelling, analytical methods, and computational many-body physics with connections to experimental validation.

thematic_fit.rationale: No thematic overlap. Position is pure condensed-matter physics theory with no spatial cognition, learning, collaboration, XR, or HCI dimensions. Explicitly excluded domain: pure machine-learning algorithms and physics simulation are not the researcher's target.

methodological_fit.rationale: Minimal methodological alignment. Position requires many-body theory and computational physics; researcher has intermediate programming (C#, Unity, beginner Python) but no background in theoretical physics, differential equations, or physics simulation frameworks. User-studies and experimental-design skills are orthogonal to this work.

growth_value.rationale: Would not close relevant capability gaps. Researcher needs to deepen spatial cognition research, collaborative systems design, user evaluation methods, and mixed-effects modelling for HCI. Theoretical physics expertise offers no trajectory toward those goals.

strategic_value.rationale: Aalto is a priority-1 institution (positive). Funding (Research Council of Finland fellowship) is stable. However, supervision and group culture are in theoretical physics, not HCI or immersive systems. No pathway to target identity as human-centred XR/HCI researcher.
